answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens to participate in an audited graph topology. When an adversarial cluster forms an isolated island, multi-agent auditing committees execute topological cut verifications. If cross-cluster trust edges collapse or falsify validation, a game-theoretic challenge triggers stake slashing. At the zenith of coordination, this imposes a superlinear attacker cost scaling with $O(n^{1.5})$ collateral per node, rendering any malicious identity a slashed relic.
